Statewide network of fire lookout towers, mostly in fire-prone forest regions
evidence.quote: Wisconsin once had a vast fire tower lookout network, mostly in the forested and most fire prone regions of the state.

evidence.supports: 119 towers at the height of use
evidence.quote: At the height of their use, 119 towers dotted the landscape.

evidence.supports: Many surviving towers built in the 1930s by Civilian Conservation Corps crews
evidence.quote: Many of the towers we see still standing today were built during the 1930s by the young men of the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.supports: In 2015 the 72 towers still in use were decommissioned
evidence.quote: In 2015, the 72 aging towers still in use were decommissioned.

sources.title: Connecting the dots: the fire towers of Wisconsin

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Only the Forest Fire Lookout Association county table names this tower; statewide context is from WJFW. Two searches found no build, staffing, removal or site-today source. An anyplaceamerica listing for 'Wilderness Lookout Tower (historical)' in Lincoln County returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Do not confuse with the Wilderness tower at Lampe, Stone County, Missouri (1936, Mark Twain National Forest, central_us_lookouts cache), a different tower. The 119-tower count conflicts with a 138 count in a Wisconsin Historical Society post seen only as a search snippet (page would not load), so it was not used. Story runs about 110 words, below the 120-word guide floor, because no source gives more.
